subject: math
intro: Mathematics feeds the quantitative professions — the people who model risk, mine data for patterns, optimise decisions and prove the ideas everyone else builds on.

roles.title: Mathematicians
roles.what: Conduct research in fundamental mathematics or apply mathematical techniques to problems in science, management and other fields — building, proving and refining the methods other quantitative professions rely on.
roles.where: The proof-driven strands are the groundwork: algebraic manipulation and circle theorems, the logic-and-proof and real-analysis lessons, and sequences and series where conjecture turns into justified argument.

roles.title: Statisticians
roles.what: Develop and apply statistical theory and methods to collect, organise, interpret and summarise numerical data, turning raw numbers into usable information — in biostatistics, business, economics or survey work.
roles.where: Unit 9 is the starter kit — averages and measures of spread, scatter diagrams, cumulative frequency and histograms — with unit 8's combined and conditional probability supplying the inference machinery.

roles.title: Actuaries
roles.what: Analyse statistical data on mortality, accident, sickness and retirement rates to build probability tables that forecast risk and liability, and set the insurance prices and reserves that guarantee future benefits can be paid.
roles.where: Probability of combined events, conditional probability and the exponential growth-and-decay topics from units 1 and 8 are the everyday tools for pricing risk and projecting liabilities decades ahead.

roles.title: Data Scientists
roles.what: Transform raw data into meaningful information using programming, data mining, machine learning and visualisation software — then interpret and report the findings so organisations can act on them.
roles.where: Interpreting statistical data, scatter diagrams and correlation in unit 9, plus graphs of functions and sketching curves in unit 2, train the core habit of reading patterns out of messy numbers and describing them precisely.

roles.title: Operations Research Analysts
roles.what: Apply mathematical modelling and optimisation methods to help management decide — finding the best routes, schedules, budgets and allocations of time, cost and resources, often as decision-support software.
roles.where: Graphs in practical situations, ratio and proportion, and solving equations and inequalities (units 1 to 3) underpin the modelling of costs, capacity and schedules; sketching curves teaches what makes a solution optimal.

roles.title: Mathematical Science Teachers, Postsecondary
roles.what: Teach courses in mathematical concepts, statistics and actuarial science at colleges and universities, often combining teaching with research into original and standardised mathematical techniques.
roles.where: This course's strand structure — number, algebra and graphs, geometry, trigonometry, probability and statistics — mirrors the sequence a university lecturer reteaches and deepens for undergraduates.
